'''Ciprian Ilie Foiaș''' (20 July 1933 – 22 March 2020) was a Romanian-American [[mathematician]]. He was awarded the [[Norbert Wiener Prize in Applied Mathematics]] in 1995, for his contributions in [[operator theory]].

== Education and career ==
Born in [[Reșița]], [[Romania]], Foiaș studied mathematics at the [[University of Bucharest]]. He completed his dissertation in 1957,<ref name=notices>{{cite journal|title=Remembrances of Ciprian Ilie Foias|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=October 2022|volume=69|issue=9|pages=1529–1545|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/202209/rnoti-p1529.pdf|doi= 10.1090/noti2545|doi-access=free|last1=Becker |first1=Robert A. |last2=Bercovici |first2=Hari |last3=Biswas |first3=Animikh |last4=Cheskidov |first4=Alexey |last5=Constantin |first5=Peter |last6=Eden |first6=Alp |last7=Frazho |first7=Art |last8=Jolly |first8=Michael |last9=Kukavica |first9=Igor |last10=Pearcy |first10=Carl |last11=Rosa |first11=Ricardo M S. |last12=Saut |first12=Jean-Claude |last13=Tannenbaum |first13=Allen |last14=Temam |first14=Roger |last15=Titi |first15=Edriss |last16=Voiculescu |first16=Dan }}</ref> but was not allowed to defend his thesis by the Communist government until 1962<ref name=obit>{{cite web | title=Obituary: Ciprian Ilie Foias|url=https://www.richardsonfuneralhome.org/obituary/Ciprian-Foias| access-date=2022-09-24}}</ref> because his father, a respected physician, had been sent to a [[Labor camp|forced labor camp]] after the communists came to power.<ref name="indiana">{{cite web|url=https://math.indiana.edu/about/inmemoriam/Foias,%20C.pdf|title=Ciprian Foias|publisher=[[Indiana University]]|website=math.indiana.edu|access-date=March 2, 2024}}</ref> He received his [[doctorate]] in 1962 from the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]] (IMAR) under supervision of [[Miron Nicolescu]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=11349}}</ref>

Foias began teaching at the University of Bucharest in 1954.<ref name=notices/> From 1958 to 1978 he was a researcher at IMAR, and from 1966 to 1978 he was a professor in the Faculty of Mathematics at the University of Bucharest.<ref name=notices/><ref name="acad">{{cite web|url=https://acad.ro/commem/doc2020/n0322-CiprianFoias.pdf|title=Prof. Ciprian Foiaș|lang=ro|publisher=[[Romanian Academy]]|website=acad.ro|access-date=March 2, 2024}}</ref> In recognition of his growing international reputation, he was named ''[[docent|doctor docent]]'' in 1968. 

Foias was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in [[Nice]] in 1970, and again at the ICM in [[Helsinki]] in 1978. Following his lecture in Helsinki, he defected to France, and then taught at the [[Paris-Sud University|University of Paris — XI]] from 1979 to 1983. He later emigrated to the United States, where he was a professor at [[Indiana University]] from 1983 until retirement. Beginning in 2000, he was a teacher and researcher at [[Texas A&M University]], where he was a Distinguished Professor.<ref name=notices/>

Together with [[Béla Szőkefalvi-Nagy]], Foias proved the celebrated [[commutant lifting theorem]]. The [[Foias constant]] is named after him. Foias is listed as an [[ISI highly cited researcher]].<ref>{{cite web|title=List of ISI highly cited researchers|url=http://highlycited.com}}</ref> In 1994 he was elected honorary member of the [[Romanian Academy]].<ref name="acad"/><ref name="acad-list">{{cite web|url=https://acad.ro/bdar/armembri.php|title=Membrii Academiei Române din 1866 până în prezent|lang=ro|publisher=[[Romanian Academy]]|website=acad.ro|access-date=March 2, 2024}}</ref>

He died in [[Tempe, Arizona]] on March 22, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://usobit.com/obituaries-2020/03/ciprian-foias-july-20-1933-march-22-2020-age-86/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200323231314/https://usobit.com/obituaries-2020/03/ciprian-foias-july-20-1933-march-22-2020-age-86/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=March 23, 2020|title=Obituary for Ciprian Foias|date=23 March 2020 |access-date=March 23, 2020}}</ref> That year, the [[American Mathematical Society]] established the Ciprian Foias Prize in Operator Theory, which is awarded every three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=48|title=Ciprian Foias Prize in Operator Theory|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]| website=www.ams.org|access-date=March 2, 2024}}</ref>

== Publications ==
* with {{ill|Ion Colojoară|ro}}: ''Theory of generalized spectral operators''. Gordon and Breach, 1968. {{MR|0394282}}
* with [[Béla Szőkefalvi-Nagy]]: ''Harmonic analysis of operators on Hilbert Space''. North Holland 1970 (Translated from the French; first edition: Masson 1967). {{MR|0275190}}
* with [[Peter Constantin]], [[Roger Temam]]: ''Attractors representing turbulent flows''. [[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 53, 1985. {{MR|0776345}}
* with Hari Bercovici, [[Carl Pearcy]]: ''Dual algebras with applications to invariant subspaces and dilation theory''. CBMS Regional Conf. Ser. in Math., vol. 56, American Mathematical Society, 1985. {{MR|0787041}}
* with Peter Constantin: ''Navier Stokes Equations''. [[University of Chicago Press]], 1988. {{ISBN|0-226-11548-8}}. {{MR|0972259}}
* with Peter Constantin, Roger Temam, and Basil Nicolaenko: ''Integral Manifolds and Inertial Manifolds for Dissipative Partial Differential Equations''. [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer-Verlag]], Applied Mathematical Sciences Series, volume 70, 1988.
* with Hitay Özbay, [[Allen Tannenbaum]]: ''Robust control of infinite dimensional systems''. Springer, 1995.
* with [[Roger Temam]], Oscar Manley, and Ricardo Rosa: ''Navier Stokes equations and Turbulence''. [[Cambridge University Press]], 2001. {{ISBN|0-521-36032-3}} {{MR|1855030}}
